title: Function Pointer Syntax
concept: A function pointer stores a function's address in a variable to switch which function runs at runtime

steps.title: Defining the add function
steps.explanation:
`add` adds two integers and returns the result.

A function name can be used like the starting address of the function in the code segment.

steps.title: Defining the sub function
steps.explanation:
`sub` performs subtraction with the same signature.

Since it shares the same signature as `add`, it can be assigned to the same function pointer.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Now we declare a function pointer and swap the target function.

steps.title: Declaring a function pointer
steps.explanation:
`int (*op)(int, int)` is a function pointer that takes two ints and returns an int.

If the parentheses are misplaced, it becomes an entirely different declaration.

steps.title: Assigning the add function's address
steps.explanation: `op = add;` makes `op` point to the add function.

steps.title: Calling add through the pointer
steps.explanation: `op(10,20)` is currently linked to add, so it returns 30.

steps.title: Reassigning to the sub function's address
steps.explanation: `op = sub;` reassigns a different function address to the same pointer.

steps.title: Calling sub through the pointer
steps.explanation: The same `op(10,20)` call now executes sub and returns -10.
steps.keyInsight: The same call expression behaves differently depending on which function the pointer targets.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
The program ends with `return 0;`.

Key point: Function pointers are a tool for swapping the execution target at runtime.

quiz.question: Which correctly declares a pointer to void func(int x)?
quiz.explanation:
The format is: return_type (*variable_name)(parameter_types).
The `(*p)` parentheses are the key.

misconceptions.wrong: Function pointers have a different memory structure than variable pointers.
misconceptions.correct:
They are variables holding 32/64-bit address values just the same.
The only difference is they point to the code segment instead of the data segment.
misconceptions.why: From the CPU's perspective, data addresses and code addresses are all just numbers.

keyTakeaway: Function pointers enable flexible design by allowing you to switch which function executes at runtime.
